Since the patient is canceling only 24 hours before the appointment, which is less than the required 48-hour notice [3], a late cancellation fee applies [1]. Because a cleaning is a hygiene appointment, the charge is **$35** [1].

Please also note that this fee may be waived if it's the first time this patient is incurring it this calendar year, at the front desk's discretion [1].
The office address is 410 Heron Lake Blvd, Suite 200, Kissimmee, FL 34741 [1].

**SunCoast PPO patient – Yes, they can come back on October 1.**
SunCoast PPO allows 2 cleanings per calendar year and only counts by calendar year with no minimum gap between visits [1][4]. Since the May 1 cleaning was their first of the year, the October 1 cleaning would be their second within the same calendar year and would be covered [1].

**BlueWave HMO patient – No, they cannot come back on October 1.**
BlueWave HMO requires that cleanings be at least **6 months apart** [4]. May 1 to October 1 is only **5 months**, so the patient does not yet meet the frequency requirement [1]. The earliest the BlueWave patient could be eligible for a second cleaning would be **November 1** (6 months after May 1). If the patient still needs a cleaning before then, the front desk must inform them of the **$120 self-pay fee** for an adult cleaning before booking [1].

**Bottom line:** The SunCoast patient is cleared for October 1; the BlueWave patient is not and would need to wait until November 1 or pay out-of-pocket [1][4].

For a hygiene (cleaning) appointment where the patient is more than 15 minutes late and must be rescheduled, that counts as a late cancellation [1]. The late cancellation fee for a hygiene appointment is **$35** [3].

So you would charge the patient **$35**.

Note: The fee can be waived once per patient per calendar year at the front desk's discretion, and is always waived for medical emergencies or county-declared severe weather [3]. Be sure to note any waiver in the patient's account notes [3].
I don't know, please check with the office manager.
The main phone number for Lakeside Family Dental is (407) 555-0142 [3].
The office is open on Friday from 7:30 AM to 1:00 PM [1].

The fee for a no-show is **$75** [1]. This applies when the patient does not arrive and does not call [1]. Please note that fees are waived once per patient per calendar year at the front desk's discretion, and medical emergencies or county-declared severe weather are always waived [1].

The three-strike rule is triggered after **three** no-shows within a 12-month period [1]. Once triggered, the patient may only book **same-day appointments** for the next **6 months** [1]. If an exception to this restriction is needed, it must be approved by the office manager [1].

New patients should arrive **15 minutes early** for their first visit [1]. This allows time to complete any remaining intake paperwork on a tablet in the waiting room, or to have their photo ID and insurance card scanned if not already uploaded [1].

The Lakeside Smile Club costs $29 per month or $299 per year [2]. It's an in-house membership designed for patients without insurance, and it covers 2 cleanings, 2 exams, 1 set of bitewing X-rays per year, plus 20% off other treatment [2].

For an in-house payment plan, you need to put **25% down**, and the remaining balance is split over a maximum of **6 months**, interest free [1]. This plan is available for treatments over $500 [1][2].
Records requests are fulfilled within **15 business days** [1].
The after-hours voicemail gives the on-call doctor's pager number as **(407) 555-0177** [1].

A patient with a knocked-out permanent tooth should come in within **60 minutes** [1]. In the meantime, they should pick the tooth up by the crown (not the root), rinse it gently, and either try to place it back in the socket or keep it in milk [1]. A knocked-out permanent tooth is considered a dental emergency [3].

A minor aged **14 to 17** may attend a routine cleaning alone (after the first visit) if a signed **Minor Attendance Form** is on file [1]. This must be a cleaning that does not involve numbing, extractions, or sedation, as a parent or guardian is still required to be present for those types of treatment [1].
The SunCoast Dental PPO annual maximum is **$1,500 per person** [1].
SunCoast PPO claims must be filed within **90 days** of the date of service [1][2].
A BlueWave patient's copay for a porcelain crown (D2740) is **$450** [1].

No, Lakeside Family Dental is **out of network** with GuardStar Dental PPO [1]. Patients may still be seen, but the office will collect the full fee at the time of service and provide the patient with a claim form, as GuardStar pays the patient directly for out-of-network claims [1].
The standard turnaround time from the lab (Coastline Dental Lab) is **10 business days** [2].
We bill the crown (D2740) on the **seat date**, not the prep date. Insurance pays on the date the crown is permanently placed [1].
The self-pay price for bitewing X-rays is **$65** [1].
Nitrous oxide (laughing gas) is $55 per visit [1].
If a new patient's blood pressure is above **180/110**, we do not treat them that day and instead refer them to their physician [2].

For a two-surface MO filling on a back tooth, you would use **CDT code D2392** (tooth-colored filling, two surfaces, back tooth) [1]. The office notes specifically clarify that "a two-surface filling like 'MO' uses D2392, not D2391" [1]. Remember to include the tooth number and both surfaces (M and O) on the claim [1].

The difference between D4341 and D4342 comes down to the number of teeth involved in the quadrant:

- **D4341** is a deep cleaning (scaling and root planing) for **4 or more teeth** in a quadrant [1].
- **D4342** is a deep cleaning for **1 to 3 teeth** in a quadrant [1].

Both codes require that a quadrant (UR, UL, LR, LL) be specified on the claim [1]. They also share the same billing requirements: perio charting showing pockets of 4 mm or more, plus recent X-rays [1]. Most insurers allow either code once per quadrant every **24 months** [1].

The self-pay office fees differ as well: D4341 is **$245 per quadrant**, while D4342 is **$175 per quadrant** [1].
For a self-pay patient, the crown is $1,250 and the core buildup adds $295, for a total office fee of **$1,545** [1].
The office is open on the **first and third Saturday of each month** only, from 8:00 AM to 12:00 PM [1]. On those Saturdays, only **hygiene appointments** are offered [1].

Based on our records, the in-network plans that require at least 6 months between cleanings are:

- **BlueWave Dental HMO** – 2 cleanings per year, at least 6 months apart [4].
- **SunState Kids** – also requires 6 months between cleanings [1].

By contrast, **SunCoast PPO** does *not* have a 6-month gap requirement; it simply allows 2 cleanings per calendar year [1][4].

SunCoast Dental PPO covers a full-mouth (or panoramic) X-ray once every **5 years** [2], while BlueWave Dental HMO covers full-mouth X-rays once every **3 years** [1]. So BlueWave actually allows the full-mouth X-ray more frequently than SunCoast does.

Under SunCoast Dental PPO, a crown on the same tooth can be replaced once every **5 years** [1]. Under GuardStar Dental PPO, the same replacement is allowed once every **7 years** per tooth [2]. So SunCoast permits crown replacement more frequently—every 5 years versus GuardStar's 7-year interval.

Lakeside Family Dental is in network with the following insurance plans:

- **SunCoast Dental PPO**
- **BlueWave Dental HMO**
- **SunState Kids program** [1]

Patients with other insurance plans, such as GuardStar Dental PPO, are seen as out of network [3].

The per-person deductible for **SunCoast Dental PPO** is **$50** (waived for preventive services) [2], while the per-person deductible for **GuardStar Dental PPO** is **$75** [1]. So SunCoast's deductible is $25 lower per person compared to GuardStar.

Adult bitewing X-rays are covered at different frequencies under the two plans:

- **SunCoast Dental PPO:** 1 set per calendar year [3].
- **GuardStar Dental PPO:** 1 set every **2 years** for adults [2].

So SunCoast covers adult bitewing X-rays twice as often as GuardStar (annually vs. every two years). Also note that Lakeside Family Dental is **out of network** with GuardStar, and the office's default recommendation is bitewings every 12 months for adults (or every 24 months for low-risk adults) [1][4].

Yes, a pre-authorization is required for this crown, and it triggers **two** rules:

1. **SunCoast PPO requirement:** Any single treatment over **$400** must be pre-authorized [2]. A $1,250 crown far exceeds that threshold.

2. **Our office policy:** Any treatment plan over **$1,000** requires a pre-authorization for *any* insurance, even if the insurer doesn't explicitly demand it, so the patient knows their cost upfront [2].

Since the crown is $1,250, both conditions are met [2]. The front desk should also note that with insurance we **never guess** the patient's cost—we go through the pre-authorization process [1].

**Quick next steps:**
- The doctor finalizes the treatment plan in ChairSide PM, and the pre-auth is submitted electronically with the same attachments a claim would need [4].
- Most insurers (including SunCoast) respond within **2 to 4 weeks** [4].
- Once the response arrives, call the patient to review their estimated cost and schedule the appointment [4].

> **Note:** If the patient has an urgent need (infection, severe pain), the treatment does **not** wait for the pre-authorization; the doctor simply documents the urgency in the chart [4].

Yes, we still send a pre-authorization. Even though BlueWave HMO only *requires* pre-authorization for specialist referrals [1], our **office policy** mandates a pre-authorization (pre-treatment estimate) for **any treatment plan over $1,000 for any insurance**, even if the insurer does not require it, so the patient knows their cost [1]. Since this plan is $1,200, it crosses that $1,000 threshold [1].

Once submitted, we let the patient know most insurers respond within **2 to 4 weeks**, and when the response arrives we call to review their estimated cost and schedule [2].

No, a porcelain crown on a back molar is **not covered** under the SunState Kids program. The program explicitly lists porcelain crowns on back teeth as a non-covered service, and stainless steel crowns are the covered alternative instead [3].

Yes, fluoride is covered for a 15-year-old SunCoast Dental PPO patient. SunCoast covers fluoride for patients under age 16, up to twice per year [2]. The office notes also remind us to check the plan's age limit of under 16 when billing fluoride varnish (D1206) [4]. Since a 15-year-old falls under that age limit, they are eligible for coverage.

A BlueWave patient who needs to see an oral surgeon must first obtain a **referral approved by BlueWave before the appointment** [1]. The approval process takes **5 to 7 business days** [1].

Additionally, before the visit, you should confirm on the BlueWave portal that the patient is still assigned to our office, since assignments can change monthly [2]. And remember that BlueWave is an HMO, so the patient must have Lakeside Family Dental listed as their assigned office for the plan to cover the visit [3].

Since GuardStar is an out-of-network plan for Lakeside Family Dental, here's how we handle the $400 filling:

- **Collect the full $400 fee at the time of service** and give the patient a claim form to submit directly to GuardStar, as GuardStar pays the patient directly for out-of-network claims rather than the office [1].
- There are **no waiting periods** to worry about [1].
- The $400 cost is **below the $500 threshold** for a payment plan, so a payment plan would not be available for this filling [4].

In short, you collect the full amount up front and hand the patient their claim form to file with GuardStar [1]. If the patient has questions about the plan, you can direct them to check their own benefits or speak with the office manager.

For a $4,000 treatment plan, here's what we can offer:

**Primary option – Third-party financing (BrightPay Health):**
Since the treatment is over $3,000, we refer the patient to our third-party financing partner, **BrightPay Health**, which offers **12- to 24-month plans** [3].

**Also available – In-house payment plan:**
Because the treatment is over $500, the in-house plan is technically available as well: **25% down** (so $1,000) with the remaining balance split over a maximum of **6 months**, interest-free [1][3].

I'd recommend presenting the BrightPay Health option first, since it's the designated path for plans over $3,000 and gives the patient a longer repayment window [3]. If the patient prefers to stay in-house, the 6-month plan is still on the table [1].

Also, if the patient doesn't have insurance, you can mention the **Lakeside Smile Club** as a membership option [2]. And since the treatment plan is over $1,000, please be sure to run a **pre-authorization** regardless of the patient's insurance carrier, per our office policy [4].

Since the patient's pain is rated 8 out of 10, which is 7 or higher, the protocol is to **book the next emergency slot today** [1]. Because there is no swelling, this does not meet the criteria for sending them to the ER (which would apply with swelling affecting breathing/swallowing, fever with facial swelling, or a jaw injury) [1][2].

As for specific appointment times available on a Tuesday, I don't know, please check with the office manager.

Also, per our script, I would still confirm the remaining triage details with the caller: which tooth or area hurts and since when, whether there's any swelling (already confirmed none), whether they have a fever, and whether the pain wakes them at night or lingers after hot or cold [3].

I will not diagnose or recommend any prescription medicine over the phone — that is the doctor's role only [1].

For an existing patient last seen 4 years ago, you would use the **comprehensive exam (D0150)**. The guidelines specify that D0150 is used for "new patients, or existing patients not seen in 3+ years" [1]. Since this patient has been away for 4 years, they meet that threshold, and D0150 is the correct code rather than the periodic exam (D0120), which is for existing patients seen within the last 3 years [1].
